Snowflake coding screening weird question
Just finished tech screening for Snowflake backend engineer role last week. Got a very weird question:

>Implement a key constraint function that takes in a list of referenced rows and a list of keys to insert. Returns if there is a constraint violation.

Spent some time with the interviewer to understand the question (I am not database focused and not interviewing just for a database engineer). So basically I confirmed with the interviewer by just implementing a set to record the referenced rows (just using list of string as inputs to simplify the question) and find violation. 

The follow-up question is how to modify the codes for sorted rows (sorted by certain column). And I answered with binary search to find the matching row.

The next follow-up is what if the input file is very big. I answered with chunking the big file and search one by one (with some skipping operation since keys are still sorted)

I am using C++ as my coding language so the question does not make much sense to me (or maybe I still didn't fully undertand the question).

Any clue what the interviewer actually wants for this question?

(Anyway, already failed the interview because of this question)

# Interview Experience | OA + 3 Rounds 

Recently went through a full interview loop and wanted to share my experience. Might help others preparing for similar roles.

## Online Assessment (OA)
- 3 questions (Medium–Hard)
- Standard DSA with focus on optimization
- Graphs + 2D DP mostly and one bit manipulation
- Time constraints made brute force approaches infeasible

## Interview Round 1 (Technical)
**Focus:** DSA + Core Java Fundamentals

- DSA:
  - Median in a sliding window of size k (data stream variant)
- OOP:
  - Diamond problem in Java
  - Interface vs Abstract Class (use-cases + differences)

**Verdict:** Medium difficulty. Strong fundamentals were enough to clear.

## Interview Round 2 (Technical)
**Focus:** DSA + OOP + Backend + Experience

- DSA:
  - Sliding window based problem involving transforming array values to a target (0s)
- OOP:
  - Conceptual clarity and real-world usage
- Backend:
  - Basic architecture and practical questions
- Experience:
  - Deep dive into past projects and decisions

**Verdict:** Medium, but covered a wide range of topics. Required clarity more than depth.

## Interview Round 3 (Director of Engineering)
**Focus:** System Thinking + Real-world Problem Solving

- Resume deep dive
- Discussion points:
  - Coding experience (e.g., “how many lines of code” type questions)
  - Preferred tech stack and reasoning
- Problem:
  - Identify broken links on a website
  - Optimize the approach
  - Extend solution to a multithreaded design

**Verdict:** Hard. Focus was on scalability, clarity, and thought process

### Round 2
We had to solve 2 DSA problems in a [Pair Programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pair_programming) format, but the platform was Google Meet for discussion and Google Docs for coding. Yes, plain **Google Docs** without any formatter or highlight, you have to take care of indentation and brackets and syntax yourself and make sure it is correct.
The interviewer started with a basic version of the problem and once you're done they'll extend and change constraints, so your code and approach has to be clean and explainable. The code won't be run, it'll be checked by logic. So if you're with the habit of running to check if it is working or not, it might be difficult.
